points.title: CPU and its job
points.must: CPU = fetches, decodes, executes instructions; contains CU, ALU, registers, cache; connected by system bus.
points.model: CPU = part of the computer that fetches, decodes and executes program instructions. Contains: control unit (CU), arithmetic logic unit (ALU), registers, cache. Connected to main memory and I/O by the system bus.

points.title: Control unit and ALU
points.must: CU decodes and sends control signals, coordinates the cycle; ALU does arithmetic and logic, result in ACC, sets flags.
points.model: CU: decodes instructions, sends control signals, coordinates the fetch–decode–execute cycle and use of the buses. ALU: arithmetic (add, subtract) and logic (AND, OR, NOT, compare, shift); result in the accumulator; sets flags.

points.title: Registers, clock, cache
points.must: Register = small fast storage inside CPU; clock sends pulses that synchronise; cache = fast memory for frequently used data.
points.model: Register = very small, very fast storage inside the CPU holding one value in use now. Clock = regular pulses that synchronise components (1 pulse = 1 clock cycle). Cache = small fast memory holding copies of frequently/recently used instructions and data.

points.title: System bus and bus width
points.must: Definition of system bus (parallel lines connecting CPU, memory, I/O controllers; 1 bit per line); bus width = number of lines.
points.model: System bus = set of parallel wires (lines) on the motherboard connecting the CPU, main memory and I/O controllers; each line carries 1 bit at a time; made of address, data and control buses. Bus width = number of lines = number of bits carried at the same time.

points.title: Shared bus: advantages and bottleneck
points.must: Shared bus is simple, cheap, expandable, but only one transfer at a time → bottleneck.
points.model: Shared bus: cheap, simple wiring, easy to add devices. But only one component can use it at a time → devices take turns → bottleneck (von Neumann bottleneck).

points.title: Address bus
points.must: Carries address of memory location / I/O port; one-way from CPU; n lines → 2ⁿ locations.
points.model: Address bus: carries the address of the memory location or I/O port to be read/written. Unidirectional (CPU → memory/I/O). n lines → 2ⁿ addressable locations; one extra line doubles memory. 32 lines → 4 GiB.

points.title: Data bus
points.must: Carries data and instructions; two-way; width = bits transferred at once.
points.model: Data bus: carries data and instructions between CPU, memory and I/O. Bidirectional (read: into CPU, write: out of CPU). Width = number of bits transferred at once (64-bit bus = 8 bytes per transfer).

points.title: Control bus and its signals
points.must: Carries control/timing signals; both directions; examples: memory read, memory write, clock, interrupt request, bus request/grant, reset.
points.model: Control bus: carries control and timing signals, both to and from the CPU. Signals: memory read, memory write, I/O read/write, clock, interrupt request, bus request / bus grant, reset.

points.title: Why address bus is one-way
points.must: Only CPU chooses the location; data must go in both directions.
points.model: Address bus one-way because only the CPU decides which location is used. Data bus two-way because data goes into the CPU (read) and out of it (write).

points.title: Address bus calculation
points.must: Worked example: 16-bit address bus → 65 536 locations = 64 KiB; 8-bit data bus → 4 reads for 4 bytes.
points.model: 16 address lines: 2¹⁶ = 65 536 locations × 1 byte = 64 KiB. 8-bit data bus: a 4-byte value needs 4 reads; a 32-bit data bus needs 1 read. More address lines → more memory, not faster transfers.

points.title: MAR and MDR
points.must: MAR holds address, connected to address bus; MDR holds data, connected to data bus.
points.model: MAR (memory address register): holds the address of the location to use, output to the address bus. MDR (memory data register): holds data read from / to be written to memory, connected to the data bus.

points.title: Memory read steps
points.must: Address into MAR → address bus; read signal on control bus; memory puts contents on data bus; data into MDR.
points.model: Memory read: 1) address placed in MAR and sent on address bus; 2) CU sends memory read signal on control bus; 3) memory puts contents of that location on data bus; 4) data copied into MDR. Memory keeps its value.

points.title: Memory write steps
points.must: Address in MAR → address bus; data in MDR → data bus; write signal on control bus; memory stores data.
points.model: Memory write: 1) address in MAR → address bus; 2) data in MDR → data bus; 3) CU sends memory write signal on control bus; 4) memory stores the data at that address (old value overwritten).

points.title: I/O transfers and DMA
points.must: I/O controllers have ports with addresses; same buses with I/O read/write; DMA moves blocks between device and memory without the CPU using bus request/grant and an interrupt.
points.model: I/O: CPU puts port address on address bus, data on data bus, I/O read/write on control bus; controllers have buffers. DMA: device sends bus request, CPU gives bus grant, DMA controller copies a block directly device ↔ memory, then interrupts the CPU. Saves CPU time for large blocks.
